growth_story.headline: Haiti's income per person has fallen every year since 2019, as gang violence and political crisis deepened a decline that began after its 1980 peak.
growth_story.arc: Haiti's income per person peaked in 1980 and is now 48.3 percent below that peak, lower even than in 1960, the first year of the record. From 1990 to 1997 it shrank by 2.3 percent a year, as the 1991 military coup brought a trade embargo and the loss of most aid that hit manufacturing hardest; after 1994 only apparel came back. From 1998 to 2017 growth averaged just 0.4 percent a year: disputed elections, the armed conflict of 2004 and the 2010 earthquake broke each recovery, and the rebuilding after the earthquake was cut short by political uncertainty. Since 2018 income per person has fallen by 3.1 percent a year, and it has dropped every year since 2019, as armed gangs grew after the 2021 assassination of the president and the stock of capital began to shrink. Over the last decade the fall averaged 2.3 percent a year, against growth of 0.8 percent a year in the decade before.

threads.title: Embargo and narrow exports
threads.text: The 1991 to 1994 trade embargo cut industry's access to imported inputs and hit manufacturing hardest. When it ended in 1994, only garments came back; other assembly exports did not.

threads.title: Recoveries cut short
threads.text: Between 1998 and 2017, a deadlock after the disputed 2000 elections, the armed conflict that removed the president in 2004 and the 2010 earthquake each interrupted growth. Rebuilding after the earthquake, backed by strong outside financing, was derailed as politics grew uncertain.

threads.text: The 2021 assassination of the president set off an institutional crisis and a power vacuum, and no general election has been held in a decade. The World Bank ties the long contraction to falling productivity as insecurity grew from 2019.

since_last_year.text: Output kept shrinking through 2026, and in 2025 income per person fell for a seventh year in a row. Hurricane Melissa struck in October 2025, US trade preferences lapsed and were then extended, the transitional council ended in February 2026 without elections, and a UN-backed force against the gangs began arriving in April 2026.

growth_story.tension: The World Bank says Haiti grew rapidly in the second half of the 1990s and that capital build-up drove growth from 2010 to 2020, but income per person shows little of this. After a 7.8 percent rebound in 1995 it grew 2.2 percent in 1996 and only 0.8, 0.3 and 0.8 percent in 1997 to 1999, and the 1998 to 2017 era averaged just 0.4 percent a year.
